item.title: Liverpool hold firm stance on youngster’s future amid interest from European giants
item.description: Liverpool hold firm stance on youngster’s future amid interest from European giants Liverpool Transfer News: Rio Ngumoha Going Nowhere Amid Bayern Munich Interest Liverpool have made their position emphatically clear on Rio Ngumoha, with the club unwilling to entertain any prospect of a sale despite reported interest from Bayern Munich and attention from across Europe. According to TeamTalk , Liverpool sources are adamant there is no intention to part with the teenager. The 18-year-old is held in the highest regard internally, with senior figures at Anfield convinced he has the attributes to become a major player for club and country in the years ahead. The message coming out of Merseyside is straightforward. Liverpool “have no intention of selling highly rated teenager Rio Ngumoha” and “any approaches for Ngumoha would be rebuffed by Liverpool”. That stance appears to apply not only to the January window, but well beyond it. Rio Ngumoha Central to Liverpool Plans There is growing conviction inside the club that Ngumoha can develop into a genuine first-team fixture. He is described as “a supreme talent capable of developing into a key player for the Reds and one of the best in Europe”, which offers a striking insight into how strongly Liverpool rate him behind the scenes. That belief has been shaped by what he has already shown. Ngumoha has impressed with his speed, technical quality and willingness to attack defenders directly, traits that have stood out in his senior opportunities. Since debuting as a 16-year-old in January 2025, he has gone on to make 43 first-team appearances and scored three goals. Liverpool’s internal view is that he is “seen as central to Liverpool’s long-term plans” and possesses “the potential to become a regular starter and a top player in both the Premier League and Champions League”. For a player still at the earliest stage of his career, that is a substantial vote of confidence. Photo: IMAGO Bayern Munich Interest Meets Firm Resistance Bayern Munich’s admiration is understood to be genuine, particularly as they assess options on the left flank. Yet Liverpool’s refusal to engage appears to have shut down any realistic chance of progress. Reports of serious interest have circulated for months, but the club’s stance “has remained firm throughout”. Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also said to be monitoring developments. Even so, no formal movement is anticipated at this stage, largely because Liverpool’s position is so entrenched and the player himself is settled. Ngumoha is understood to be happy at the club and focused on continuing his rise under Andoni Iraola. That matters. Liverpool want elite young players to see a pathway, and this situation suggests Ngumoha believes his future is best served by staying put. item.title: Thomas Tuchel bemoans Cole Palmer availability by not selecting Cole Palmer when available
item.description: The latest England squad was announced this morning, and once again it only contains one Chelsea player, Morgan Rogers, with Tuchel-favorite Reece James injured and Tuchel-unfavorite Cole Palmer left at home. The Palmer thing is starting to approach extra silly levels now, with the former Chelsea head coach explaining that he didn’t pick the Chelsea starboy due to his previous unavailability. I bet Tuchel wouldn’t hesitate to pick Reecey in the same situation — in fact, we kind of know he wouldn’t — so perhaps he just needs to come out and say that he doesn’t rate Palmer, rather than continuing to insinuate that Palmer isn’t committed enough to the national team, or some other such nonsense. “We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together. We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He is kind of an extra player and he can play all four positions. “I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress.” -Thomas Tuchel; source: BBC Well, he certainly ain’t gonna impress if you don’t pick him! Might as well be a meme at this point. On the plus side, Palmer now gets to kick his feet up for a couple weeks, play some video games, and be fully rested as we head into the fixture crunch of winter and the holiday period. item.description: Former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers, fresh off his induction into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame and rejoining the NBA media space as a game analyst for NBC Sports in September, took a long look back at his time coaching the Bucks for 2 ½ seasons on a Bill Simmons podcast episode released Nov. 6 . In the 2-hour, 33-minute episode, Rivers went into great detail about coaching former Bucks superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo , whom the team traded to Miami on July 6 after a 13-year run that included a championship and Antetokounmpo earning top-75 status as one of the greatest players in league history. Rivers replaced Adrian Griffin as head coach midseason in 2023-24 and compiled a 97-103 record with the Bucks. Milwaukee did not advance out of the first round of the 2024 and 2025 playoffs and went 32-50 last season. The Bucks and Rivers parted ways afterward with one year left on his contract. After the deal with Miami was agreed upon, the Journal Sentinel published a detailed report about how and why the organization decided to trade Antetokounmpo , and the deteriorating relationship between Rivers and the star player had a significant role. Rivers addressed many of the topics that were previously written about, for the first time in the podcast. Here's a look at some of the topics: Bill Simmons attended the Miami game against the Los Angeles Clippers on Nov. 5 in Los Angeles and commented on weird vibes with the Heat despite a comeback victory. There’s certain type of things that have to happen. Spacing has to always be right. And you feel like you’re in the way as a player with Giannis if you’re in the wrong space. And he feels like you’re in the way if you don’t have the right spacing. Having been suspended by Spire Motorsports earlier in the week, which predated a $100,000 fine and 25-point deduction, Hocevar was required to do a press conference taking every question on the topic. In this moment, Hocevar was stripped of his usual boyish exuberance and dryly answered each question that came his way. item.description: Mar 29, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Miami Heat forward Andrew Wiggins (22) in the second half against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. But nine games in? It just hasn’t clicked . They’re 3-6 and coming off a flat 120-100 loss to Golden State, where Andrew Wiggins had two points on six shots in 21 minutes. Nobody’s panicking in early November, but if you’re looking at why this offense feels so cramped , Wiggins is right in the center of the frame. He’s struggling with 8.6 PPG while shooting 40.8% overall and 29.7% from deep. Last year, he gave them 15.4 points a night on 41.4% from three. In a vacuum, slumps happen. But on a wing next to two paint-dominant stars, those empty calories hurt fast. Giannis is doing his thing (27.3 PPG, 12.5 RPG) and Bam is putting up 18.6 and 8.0, but the overall flow isn’t there, mainly due to the Heat’s lack of an outside threat, with Tim Hardaway Jr. also at 24.3% from 3. Pairing Giannis and Bam was always going to test Miami’s spacing. Bam is hitting under 18% of his threes, and as a team, Miami is 21st with 33.1% from deep. The good news for Pat Riley is that Wiggins can be a pretty sweet trade chip. His contract ($30.2M this year before his extension kicks in at $16.5M in 2027-28) is a massive, flexible matching salary to move right now without creating long-term cap headaches. This is part of the inevitable evolution of the college landscape, as the NCAA decided to allow for “five-for-five” this past offseason. Five-for-five plays out exactly how you think. College players have five years of service available to them before they’ve exhausted their NCAA eligibility, no matter whether they took a redshirt year or not. What this means is that true seniors, players who got on the field for four years without burning a redshirt, are no longer getting pushed out of the NCAA, but actually have another year of eligibility. I first got wind of this upcoming trend in October, so I decided to look at the upcoming class and how it would impact it. My finding: It could impact it a lot. item.description: Leeds United Linked With This Liverpool Player: Should They Sign Him? Leeds United have turned themselves into one of the Premier League’s most awkward opponents, a direct, physical side closer to Everton’s scrap-and-set-piece approach than to a passing team. Daniel Farke’s players sit 12th with 11 points from nine matches, built on two wins, five draws and two defeats, the latest coming away at Bournemouth . Leeds lead the division for duels won, interceptions and headed clearances, and they draw more than 40 per cent of their expected goals from set-pieces. That approach follows a 14th-place finish last season, though victories have dried up lately. In the summer, Leeds signed striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, winger Harry Wilson and defender Tarik Muharemovic, all physically imposing. Farke’s 4-2-3-1 asks for a brave build-up, yet most transitions go straight to a big front-runner or an isolated wide outlet. Behind Calvert-Lewin, Brenden Aaronson holds the central creative role. He has made eight appearances, five from the bench, and brings intense pressing without much goal threat. On the right, Wilson has started seven games as a left-footed runner who cuts inside, with Daniel James also available. Football Insider’s Pete O’Rourke reports that Leeds have fresh encouragement to sign long-term target Harvey Elliott permanently in January. The 23-year-old Liverpool midfielder has not started a match on loan at Valencia and recently saw red for dissent, so the Spanish club is preparing to end the loan early. Andoni Iraola, the Liverpool manager, does not include him in his plans, and Liverpool want a permanent sale rather than another loan. Elliott works as a number 10 or an inverted right winger. He brings elite spatial intelligence in the half-spaces, a delicate weight of pass and high creative volume, but he lacks top-end recovery speed and struggles in physical and aerial duels. That clashes with a Leeds side leading the league in the exact metrics he cannot supply. item.title: Trading Robert Hunt Fixes Cap, Hurts Panthers Depth
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Carolina Panthers face a tough choice before the November 10 deadline. They can keep underperforming star Robert Hunt or trade him to fix their money problems. According to Cat Crave , moving Hunt would solve a major financial headache but create a huge hole in the starting lineup. General manager Dan Morgan must decide if saving cash is worth losing a Pro Bowl player who is not playing like one right now. The Money Problem Gets Worse Hunt signed a massive five-year, $100 million deal in 2024 free agency. That contract looked great when he was forming a top guard tandem with Damien Lewis. The 2020 second-round pick counts $24.3 million against the salary cap. If the Panthers cut him, they still owe $10.3 million in dead money after restructured deals. Trading him now saves much more. ESPN beat reporter Mike Kaye noted that a trade involving Hunt would release $19 million in cap space for next year. The offensive line is already a mess. Cat Crave points out that Carolina does not have enough depth to trade Hunt without making things worse. The team is somehow still leading the NFC South, but that lead could vanish fast if the line collapses. Hunt is being paid like a top-tier interior lineman. He is simply not playing like one anymore. A torn bicep last season dented his momentum, and he has not been the same player since. The excuse of playing next to rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling does not really hold up for a man on his contract. What Other Teams Paid Mike Kaye also pointed to recent trades for Cam Jurgens and Quenton Nelson as a reason to consider moving Hunt. Those players both warranted historic hauls in midseason swaps. Should the price be correct, it might be prudent to consider parting ways with the 2024 Pro Bowl lineman. But the Panthers are in a precarious situation. Having invested heavily to reach legitimate contention, their situation is not progressing as planned. You can blame the injuries, but every team gets them. Removing Hunt from the equation would not be the smartest move regardless of how poorly he plays. His slump is alarming, yet the cost of losing him on the field might be higher than the cost of keeping him. Given his disappointing form, it is unlikely any team will offer a deal Morgan cannot refuse. The next game is Sunday, Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET, when the Denver Broncos visit Bank of America Stadium.

item.title: Kimi Antonelli fastest in Friday practice for Sao Paulo Grand Prix
item.description: Italian Formula One driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli of team Mercedes drives during free practice one at the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Kimi Antonelli fastest in Friday practice for Sao Paulo Grand Prix») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa New world champion Kimi Antonelli topped the charts in Friday practice for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. The 20-year-old became Formula One's youngest champion last weekend, clinching the title with third place in Mexico. Antonelli admits he has not arrived in Brazil in the best of shape after the celebrations but immediately showed strong pace. The 20-year-old was pipped by the man he replaced as champion - Lando Norris - in the day's opening session but turned the tables to finish Friday 0.253 seconds clear of the McLaren driver. McLaren have brought a significant upgrade package to Interlagos, in a bid to end the season strongly and put their car in a positive place for the start of next year. Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate George Russell, now down to fourth in the championship, will start this weekend's race with a five-place grid drop due to an engine change. The British driver was fourth fastest. Mercedes can wrap up the constructors' championship this weekend if they outscore Ferrari by three points. Max Verstappen - winner of three of the last four races - finished the day in third, a place ahead of Oscar Piastri. Charles Leclerc returned for FP2 after missing the first session. The Monegasque has been back home for the birth of his first child, while Lewis Hamilton continued the criticism of his Ferrari team-mate on Thursday. Hamilton was furious with Leclerc for a lap-one move in Mexico last weekend, questioning the 29-year-old's mentality. The seven-time world champion vowed not to be silenced as he arrived in Brazil, suggesting Leclerc races against him differently to how he approaches other drivers. Hamilton and Leclerc were well off the pace, finishing the day sixth and seventh respectively - with Leclerc over seven tenths adrift of Antonelli. Interlagos usually brings extreme weather, with potential for storms disrupting Saturday's qualifying and Sunday's race, and the mist rolled in as practice drew to a close. Rafael Camara ended the day 16th on his F1 debut for Haas. The Brazilian, current F2 leader who will drive full-time for the American side next season, has been parachuted in after Frenchman Esteban Ocon was removed from the team. Ocon admitted to a disagreement with the team during last weekend's round in Mexico, where he was withdrawn midway through, and Haas have confirmed he will not drive for them again. Camara, 21, will finish his first day in F1 with a trip to the stewards for impeding Leclerc.

item.title: Miami Carol City officially out of FHSAA football playoffs after judge denies injunction
item.description: A last-minute legal effort by 11 Miami Carol City football players and their respective guardians to overturn the program’s postseason ban was denied Friday, Nov. 6, keeping the Chiefs out of the 2026 Florida high school football playoffs. The lawsuit, filed Wednesday, Nov. 4, in Miami-Dade Circuit Court , challenged the Florida High School Athletic Association's decision to exclude the Chiefs from the 2026 high school football playoffs following an Oct. 2 postgame altercation with Grayson (GA). Miami-Dade Circuit Judge Antonio Arzola reviewed the plaintiffs' motion for an emergency temporary injunction and denied the request Friday. The decision leaves the FHSAA's postseason ban in place. The denial of the emergency injunction does not resolve the underlying dispute over whether the FHSAA's postseason ban unfairly penalizes players who were not involved in the altercation. The 11 players and their guardians argued that the association's decision amounted to collective punishment and violated Florida law. The plaintiffs sought an injunction that would allow players who were not individually suspended to participate in the postseason. They did not seek to overturn the individual suspensions imposed on 15 Carol City players. The FHSAA placed Carol City on restrictive probation, excluding the program from the 2026-27 football postseason, and also imposed a $1,500 fine and required the school to host an athletic department compliance workshop. The association's board of directors denied the school's appeal Sunday, Nov. 1. It was not immediately clear whether the plaintiffs planned to pursue additional legal action. The ruling came on the same day the FHSAA was scheduled to release its 2026 football playoff brackets, which are set for 5 p.m. Friday. item.title: Kerby Joseph looks 'awesome' at Lions practice in return from knee injury
item.description: Kerby Joseph “looked awesome” in his first team reps in more than a year, and Detroit Lions safeties coach Jim O’Neil said the team still is figuring out how and when to work him back into the defense. “Those are all conversations [to be had],” O’Neil said Friday, Nov. 6, in Allen Park. “Again, the focus right now is let’s see if we can stack some days. Let’s see if he can look like he looked yesterday for three or four days in a row.” Joseph has not played since Oct. 12, 2025, at Kansas City, because of a cartilage condition in his knee . Joseph returned to practice last week for the first time since December, took part primarily in individual drills and graduated to team reps for the first time Thursday. O’Neil said Joseph “looked a lot better than what I anticipated” in practice Thursday. “I just didn’t know,” O’Neil said. “It’s been a year. It’s been a year since he’s been on the grass and it’s been a year-and-three-quarters since he’s really played at a Pro Bowl, high level cause he was fighting that thing for six or seven weeks last year so you just didn’t know. And again, he’s worked his ass off. He has. And he’s gone through a mental battle, he’s gone through a physical battle and he’s in a great place right now and I’m excited for him.” UPDATE: Jack Campbell 'continues to improve,' Lions down starters vs Dolphins The Lions could wait until after their game in Germany next week to activate Joseph to the 53-man roster, though it remains unclear what role he’ll have when he returns. He is out for Sunday's game at Miami. Chuck Clark has started every game at safety this season, and Brian Branch returned to the lineup two weeks ago after missing the start of the season recovering from a torn Achilles tendon. Joseph was one of the best safeties in the NFL when healthy – he leads the league with 20 interceptions since 2022 – but as part of his return-to-practice process, he and the Lions are trying to assess how his knee will hold up to the pounding of a full practice week while also knocking off the rust from 13 months without games. O’Neil said Joseph’s first practice Thursday “was very encouraging.” “Two weeks ago it was classroom work where we were really locked in, then it was walk-through and individual,” O’Neil said. “Yesterday was his first team practice and he looked a lot better than what I anticipated him to look like, so it was very encouraging. So now he’s got to stack multiple days. He’s got to stack them, so today will be a big day for him. But he looked awesome yesterday in practice.” Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com .
